seoTitle: Headless Browser Signal Tester: What Bot Detectors See
metaDescription: See which automation signals your own browser exposes, such as navigator.webdriver, HeadlessChrome, missing plugins and software rendering.
intro: Reads the signals simple bot detectors check in your browser and says which look automated.
why:
Bot detection starts with simple checks: does the browser report webdriver, does the user agent say Headless, are there plugins and languages, is there a real window size, what graphics renderer is used.

The page reads these from your own browser and explains each. A clean result proves nothing: modern automation hides most of these and detectors use many more signals. A flagged result can be a false alarm, for example with privacy extensions or unusual setups. Nothing is sent anywhere.
howTo: Open the page in the browser you want to test.
Compare a normal and an automated browser.
Use it to debug false positives on your site.

faq.q: Does a clean result mean I look human?
faq.a: No. Detectors use timing, behaviour and network signals too.

faq.q: Why does a real browser sometimes flag?
faq.a: Privacy extensions, containers and software rendering can trigger signals.
It shows what is checked; it does not help hide it.
